subject: POC trial environment options and next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: POC trial environment options and next steps

Hi Taylor / Sara,

Thanks again for a productive call earlier  appreciate the clear context on your evaluation goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped: 

Summary of success criteria (as I heard it):
- End-to-end throughput: sustain 200 qps at P99 latency < 250ms for single-request generation workload.
- Cost target: unit token cost competitive with your current baseline (looking to understand current ~$/1k tokens to benchmark).
- Data controls: logs must be retained for 30 days and routed to your SIEM for audit.
- Integration: send requests from your staging VPC, ability to call webhooks for moderation and observability.

Evaluation plan / timeline (proposal):
1) Environment decision & kickoff  choose between Hosted sandbox, Dedicated sandbox, or VPC-hosted trial by EOD Thu (2027-08-12).
2) Technical kickoff  internal tech deep-dive (Dev + infra) within 3 business days of decision.
3) Run 2-week workload run with synthetic and sample production traces.
4) Post-trial review and SOW + commercial next steps the week after trial completes.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (AM) and Dev (technical lead) for environment setup and baseline configs.
- Acme AI: Taylor (POC owner) and Sara (security/compliance) to validate networking and data controls.

Questions / decisions needed from Acme:
- Which environment do you prefer for the initial trial: Hosted sandbox (fastest), Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity), or VPC trial (your network, recommended if you need strict egress controls)?
- Do you have a preferred maintenance window for us to schedule the technical kickoff?

I can pull together a one-page SOW draft and a short network requirements checklist once you confirm the environment choice.

Thanks  happy to hop on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Marissa  great summary. Quick notes from our side: 

- Success criteria look good. We'll confirm the current token/$ baseline before the kickoff (Sara keying that).
- Shortlist on environment: leaning toward a Dedicated sandbox for the run (we want predictable throughput and isolation), but we have a couple of security questions about data egress and key management before we lock that in.

Specific asks before we decide:
1) Can Redwood provide the network requirements and the options for KMS/HSM integration?
2) For Dedicated sandbox, what's the expected lead time for provisioning a reserved pool sized for ~200 qps?
3) If we start in Hosted sandbox to accelerate time-to-start, would there be a seamless path to migrate to Dedicated later in the POC?

If you can share the network checklist and SOW draft, we'll get our security team to review and aim to confirm environment choice by EOD Thu.

 Taylor
Taylor Nguyen

Hi Taylor / Sara  quick technical note and attached checklist to help you decide: 

Short answers up front:
- Network/KMS: we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and extern HSM integrations via KMIP for Dedicated and VPC trials. Hosted sandbox supports Redwood-managed KMS (recommended for fastest start) and customer-managed KMS via cross-account roles in some cases.
- Provisioning lead time: Dedicated sandbox pool for the size you're describing is typically 35 business days once the order is approved and we have CIDR/VPC peering info.
- Migration path: yes, Hosted -> Dedicated is a supported migration path; we preserve model versions and can migrate KV cache warmup snapshots depending on workload characteristics, but there is a short reconciliation window.

Network checklist (high level)  attached as a stub below:
- IP ranges to whitelist (we will provide a list; require static egress for VPC peering)
- Ports: 443 outbound TLS for API; optional 22 for SSH to jumpbox if you're enabling maintenance access.
- VPC peering / Transit Gateway: supported for Dedicated & VPC trials.
- NAT and egress controls: for Hosted sandbox we provide restricted egress; for VPC trial we rely on customer routing.
- Certificate / mTLS options for inbound webhooks (optional)

Attached: Network_Reqs.pdf (short checklist) and a SOW draft Marissa referenced.

If you want, we can provision a small Hosted sandbox tomorrow to begin smoke tests while you do the security review for Dedicated. That would let us start measuring baseline latency and costs immediately.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
